QUARTERLY INVENTORY AUDIT REPORT
Meridian Distribution Center -- Q3 Cycle Count
Prepared by: Warehouse Operations, Audit Team 2
Date: September 20, 2024

1. Purpose and Methodology
This report documents the results of the Q3 physical inventory cycle count for eight
high-velocity SKUs stored in Zones B and C of the Meridian Distribution Center. Physical counts
were performed by two independent counters on September 18-19, 2024, and reconciled against the
warehouse management system (WMS) records as of the close of business on September 17, 2024.
Per Inventory Control Policy 6.2, any SKU whose physical count comes in more than 5% below its
system-recorded count is automatically flagged for a loss investigation, which may include
reviewing receiving logs, cycle count history, and camera footage from the relevant storage
zone. SKUs within the 5% tolerance are considered normal variance (breakage, counting error,
etc.) and are not flagged.

2. Background
Zones B and C have historically shown higher variance than the rest of the facility due to high
pick frequency and a mix of full-case and each-pick locations. The last full cycle count,
conducted in Q2, did not surface any flags, though two SKUs not in this quarter's sample came
close to the 5% line. Staff turnover in Zone C during August is noted as a possible contributing
factor to this quarter's results, though the audit team makes no determination of cause for any
individual SKU below -- that is left to the loss-investigation process for flagged items.

3. Findings by SKU
Counts below reflect the system count as of the 9/17 close of business, followed by the physical
count recorded during the 9/18-19 count.

SKU-100 (Widget Bracket, Small): system count 800 units; physical count 790 units. The 10-unit
gap is within normal handling variance for a fast-moving small-parts SKU and is not flagged.

SKU-101 (Widget Bracket, Large): system count 450 units; physical count 430 units. This is a
slightly larger percentage gap than SKU-100 but still comes in under the 5% flagging line, so no
investigation is opened.

SKU-102 (Hex Coupler, 3/4in): system count 1,200 units; physical count 1,100 units. This is the
largest raw unit gap found in Zone B this quarter. The percentage shortfall here crosses the 5%
threshold in Policy 6.2, which means this SKU is automatically flagged for loss investigation
regardless of any other factors -- receiving logs and the September camera footage for the Hex
Coupler bin will be pulled as the first step.

SKU-103 (Gasket Set, Standard): system count 300 units; physical count 295 units. A small,
unremarkable gap, well within tolerance.

SKU-104 (Bracket Mount, Steel): system count 600 units; physical count 560 units. This SKU's
shortfall percentage also crosses the 5% line and is flagged for investigation, though the raw
unit gap is smaller than SKU-102's.

SKU-105 (Gasket Set, Heavy Duty): system count 220 units; physical count 218 units. Negligible
variance.

SKU-106 (Hex Coupler, 1/2in): system count 900 units; physical count 870 units. Below the
flagging threshold; attributed to normal each-pick rounding.

SKU-107 (Bracket Mount, Aluminum): system count 150 units; physical count 120 units. Despite
being the smallest SKU by volume in this sample, this one shows by far the largest percentage
shortfall of the group, well past the 5% line, and is flagged for investigation.

4. Process Notes
Two counters independently counted each bin and reconciled differences of more than 2 units on
the spot before submitting final numbers, so the figures above already reflect a second count
where needed. The WMS system counts were not adjusted for any receiving activity between the
9/17 close of business and the physical count window; operations has confirmed no receipts
posted for these eight SKUs during that window, so the comparison is apples-to-apples.

5. Summary and Next Steps
Of the eight SKUs reviewed this cycle, a total of approximately 210 units of shrinkage were
identified across the group, concentrated in Zone B. Three SKUs will move forward to the formal
loss-investigation process per Policy 6.2; the remaining five are closed out as normal variance
with no further action. Audit Team 2 will reconvene with Zone C leads next week to review
staffing and cycle-count cadence given the turnover noted in Section 2.

questions.notes: SKU-102 (8.33%), SKU-104 (6.67%) and SKU-107 (20%) each exceed 5%; the other five do not.
